references.text: Parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:19-21|Matthew 22:19-21] where Jesus asks to see a coin and questions whose image and inscription is on it, and they answer, "Caesar's".
Parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:15-17|Mark 12:15-17] where Jesus asks for a denarius and questions whose image and inscription is on it, with the same answer: "Caesar's".

Jesus asks whose "εἰκών" (image) is on the coin. In [ref:1 Mos 1:26-27|Genesis 1:26-27] God created humankind in His image (Hebrew: tselem). The contrast between Caesar's image on the coin and God's image in humanity is an important theological undertone in Jesus' response.
In [ref:Rom 13:7|Romans 13:7], Paul urges giving to Caesar what belongs to Caesar—taxes to whom taxes are due—which reflects Jesus' teaching about rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's.
In [ref:Matt 17:24-27|Matthew 17:24-27], Jesus also addresses the issue of paying taxes, showing that one should pay what is required while revealing His freedom as God's Son.
